intro: Mars 3 touched down in Terra Sirenum on December 2, 1971 — the first lander to survive Martian atmospheric entry and reach the surface, two weeks after sister Mars 2 crashed. Communications stopped after 14.5 seconds, returning a single partial degraded greyscale image fragment. The lander likely arrived in the middle of a planet-encircling dust storm. Mars 3's exact resting location is still debated; HiRISE imaged candidate hardware in 2013.

Cutaway diagram of the Mars 3 lander hardware — the basic design heritage informed later Soviet-era Venera and Mars hardware.
Proton-K with Blok-D upper stage prepared at Baikonur Cosmodrome — 6-month transit to Mars.
HiRISE detail of the candidate Mars 3 hardware site in Terra Sirenum — released 2013 by NASA/UA HiRISE team, identified by Russian amateur space historians.
The single fragmentary image returned by Mars 3 — 79 lines, no horizon, no detail. The first picture from another planet's surface, however faint.
